newsitem.title: USA: LG&E Power Marketing signs Northwest supply deals.
newsitem.headline: LG&E Power Marketing signs Northwest supply deals.

text.p: LG&E Power Marketing (LPM) announced Thursday agreements to deliver energy to several public utilities in the U.S. Northwest which have sought to diversify from dependence on the Bonneville Power Administration for their electricity.
LG&E Power Marketing, headquartered in Fairfax, Virginia, is a subsidiary of Louisville, Kentucky-based LG&E Energy Corp. The firm's western region marketing office is in Costa Mesa, Calif.
The company said it will deliver power for four years to Washington state's Public Utility District (PUD) No.1 of Lewis County and PUD No.3 of Mason County.

A second sales schedule calls for deliveries for five years to PUD No.1 of Clallam County, PUD No.1 of Pacific County, PUD No.1 of Mason County, the City of Ellensburg and Peninsula Light Co, and a third schedule is for deliveries over seven years to the City of Port Angeles.
The deliveries will range from one to 18 megawatts (MW), depending upon the customer and month and year of delivery over the term of the contract, which began Oct 1, LPM said.

In separate agreements, LG&E Power Marketing will deliver 14 MW of power to four members of Western Montana Electric Generating and Transmission Cooperative Inc under five-year agreements, which also began Oct 1.
LPM also signed five-year contracts to deliver one and four MW, respectively, to Idaho County Light and Power Cooperative and to Vera Water and Power in Washington.
Finally, LG&E Power Marketing signed a three-year agreement, which began October 1, to deliver 10 megawatts to Public Utility District No. 1 of Benton County.
